title: Amid AI Boom, “Risk Is Spreading Throughout the Economy”: Astra Taylor & Naomi Klein
content:
We’re joined by Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor, co-authors of the book End Times Fascism, for a wide-ranging conversation on the multitrillion-dollar global investment in artificial intelligence and its reverberating effects around the world.

Klein recently spoke at the People’s AI Assembly, alongside other critics of the artificial intelligence industry, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and former chair of the Federal Trade Commission Lina Khan. “The resistance to AI is taking many forms, and it’s really a resistance to oligarch power, which is concentrated in the hands of these tech companies,” Klein tells Democracy Now! “After 50 years of outsourcing and hollowing out of public functions of the state, the very last stage is the outsourcing of thinking, of intelligence itself.”

Watch the full segment here.

title: Zohran Mamdani Backs Major Expansion of New York’s Data Center Moratorium
content:
Speaking on stage at the AI Now Institute and More Perfect Union’s “People’s AI Assembly,” actress and advocate Ilana Glazer asked the New York City mayor if he would push Gov. Hochul to sign the “Responsible Data Center Development Act,” which passed New York state legislation earlier this year; Mamdani responded with a simple and resolute “yes.”

[…]

Numerous surveys find that anti-AI and specifically anti-data-center sentiments have grown nationwide over the past year. This collective anxiety over AI development was palpable on Monday night at the “People’s AI Assembly,” where the entry line at New York City’s Webster Hall wrapped comfortably around the block. Attendees included college students holding “no data center” signs in hand, concerned parents of school-age children facing a future seemingly inundated with AI, and even some tech workers employed by the very companies selling the technology.

title: Mamdani says feds have abdicated on AI, urges New Yorkers to push back
content:
Two of New York’s sweethearts, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and activist and “Broad City” star Ilana Glazer, spoke about AI at Webster Hall in Manhattan on Monday night, with Glazer posing questions to the mayor about the future of AI in society.  

[…]

His message came at a moment when the federal government is doing little to regulate AI, leaving cities to act on their own. At The People’s AI Assembly, an event hosted by the AI Now Institute, a think tank that explores the social implications of AI, Mamdani argued that the technology’s rapid rollout is not inevitable and that public officials should hold AI companies accountable.

title: The $5 Trillion AI Bet You’re Already Paying For
content:
The people building AI say it poses an existential risk. Amba Kak thinks the bigger danger is not the machines, but the monopolies that own them, and that governments may already be slowly bailing them out.

Amba Kak is Co-Executive Director of the AI Now Institute, a former Senior Advisor on AI at the US Federal Trade Commission and a member of New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s transition team.

To make good on the roughly $5 trillion of AI spending committed over the next five years, Bain estimates the industry would need close to $2 trillion in annual revenue, more than the entire global enterprise software market.

If that revenue does not arrive, who is on the hook?

Amba explains why AI investment is moving from Big Tech’s cash reserves into debt markets that reach our 401(k)s and insurance policies, and why she believes a “slow bailout” is already underway.

Watch the full episode here.

title: AI Now’s Aashna Agarwal Testifies before NYC Council Committee of the Whole
content:
On Monday, October 5th, 2026, AI Now Program Associate Aashna Agarwal testified before the New York City Council at a Committee of the Whole hearing on the concrete risks of AI acceleration. In her testimony, Aashna outlined three critical ways that AI companies’ capital interests conflict with safeguarding the public from the risks posed by the very technology they are developing, and called on the Council to use its power and leverage to protect New Yorkers:

  • Maximize friction when it comes to the integration of AI into sensitive social domains.
  • Remedy and redress the harms AI has brought to New Yorkers already.
  • Resist the concentration of power in the AI industry and the single points of failure it creates, which put public safety and the resilience of City infrastructure at risk.

title: How the bad science of AI doomerism is good for big business
content:
There is no clear path showing that today’s AI systems will lead to superintelligence, much less a basis for calculating the probability of doom.

The power attributed to superintelligence has led some in these communities to describe advanced AI in God-like terms. […] “They believe in the advent of an almighty powerful AI god, which will either lead to destruction of humanity or help us achieve utopia,” says Boyan Milanov, Senior Research Scientist at AI Now Institute.

“What we have to keep in mind is that all this doomerism isn’t based on any scientific work,” says Milanov. “It really is science fiction. None of the claims are scientifically verifiable or falsifiable.”

title: AI Almost Started a U.S.–China War — and No One Seems to Care
content:
“Despite incessant warnings from AI companies that AI is harmful, even in hypothetical ways, they are in fact promoting that their unreliable products be instrumented within national and safety-critical infrastructure, such as defense and nuclear,” Heidy Khlaaf, chief scientist at the AI Now Institute and former systems safety engineer at OpenAI, told The Intercept. “Given AI’s lack of reliability and accuracy in such critical context, that is what will ultimately lead to a catastrophic accident. However, if such issues were acknowledged, that wouldn’t be profitable for AI companies and would slow down adoption.”

Read the full article here.
